column2: 中古英语 serchen ← 古法语 cerchier ← 晚期拉丁语 circāre（绕行寻找），源自 circus（圈）
column3: to look carefully in order to find something
column5: They searched the whole house twice.|The search lasted until midnight.
column6: going round and round a place to find something – 绕着一处反复找
column7: 搜寻：为找到某物而仔细查看|搜查：为查获而正式检查

column2: 中古英语 see-syde，由 sea ＋ side 复合而成
column3: the land beside the sea, especially as a holiday place
column5: They spent August at the seaside.|A small seaside town lies north.
column6: the land lying along the sea – 沿着海的那一侧陆地
column7: 海边：紧靠海的一带|海滨：可供游憩的滨海地区

column2: 中古英语 sesoun ← 古法语 seson（播种时节）← 拉丁语 satiō（播种），源自 serere（播）
column3: one of the four divisions of the year, or a suitable time
column5: Spring is my favourite season here.|Mangoes are cheap in season.
column6: the stretch of the year fit for a task – 一年中适合某事的那一段
column7: 季节：一年四分之一的时段|时节：适合某事的时候

column2: 古英语 sǣte ← 原始日耳曼语 *sētiją ← 原始印欧语 *sed-（坐）
column3: a place made for sitting, or a place in an assembly
column5: She took the seat by the window.|The party lost twelve seats.
column6: a place set aside for sitting – 留出来供人坐的位置
column7: 座位：供人坐下的地方|席位：议会或团体中的名额

column2: 中古英语 secret ← 古法语 secret ← 拉丁语 sēcrētus（分开的、隐藏的），为 sēcernere（分出）的过去分词
column3: something kept from others, or kept from others
column5: She kept the secret for years.|They held a secret meeting upstairs.
column6: set apart from common knowledge – 从众人所知里分出去藏起来
column7: 秘密：不让别人知道的事|秘密的：不公开进行的

column2: 中世纪拉丁语 secrētārius（受托掌管秘密者）← 拉丁语 secrētus（隐秘的），源自 secernere（分出）
column3: a person who handles letters and records for an office
column5: The secretary typed the whole report.|He works as a company secretary.
column6: one trusted with private papers – 被托付机要文书的人
column7: 秘书：办理文书事务的职员|书记：担任记录与文书的职务

column2: 古英语 sēon ← 原始西日耳曼语 *sehwan ← 原始日耳曼语 *sehwaną
column3: to notice with the eyes, or to understand
column5: I saw her cross the street.|Now I see what you mean.
column6: taking something in through the eyes – 用眼把东西接进来
column7: 见到：用眼睛觉察到|明白：在心里看清道理

column2: 古英语 sēċan ← 原始西日耳曼语 *sōkijan ← 原始日耳曼语 *sōkijaną
column3: to try to find or obtain something
column5: They sought shelter from the rain.|She seeks advice before deciding.
column6: following a trace towards what one wants – 循着线索去取所要的
column7: 寻求：设法找到或得到|追求：持续努力以求达到

column2: 中古英语 semen ← 古诺尔斯语 sœma（合宜、相称）← 原始日耳曼语 *sōmijaną（合一、相配）
column3: to give the impression of being something
column5: He seems tired this morning.|The plan seemed simple at first.
column6: fitting an impression without being confirmed – 与印象相合但未经确认
column7: 似乎：从表面看像是|显得：呈现出某种样子

column2: 借自拉丁语 sēgregātus，为 sēgregāre（分离）的过去分词，由 sē-（分开）＋ grex（群）构成
column3: to keep one group apart from another
column5: The school no longer segregates pupils.|Waste is segregated before collection.
column6: setting one part away from the flock – 把一部分从群里分出去
column7: 隔离：使两方彼此不接触|分开：把混在一起的分成几份

column2: 中古英语 seisen ← 古法语 seisir（占有）← 早期中世纪拉丁语 sacīre（提出主张）← 法兰克语 *sakjan（提起诉讼）
column3: to take hold of something suddenly and firmly
column5: He seized the rope with both hands.|Troops seized the bridge at dawn.
column6: laying claim to something by taking it – 一把拿下以主张所有
column7: 抓取：突然用力握住|夺取：以强力取得

column2: 中古英语 seldom ← 古英语 seldan ← 原始西日耳曼语 *seldanā ← 原始日耳曼语 *seldanē
column3: not often
column5: He seldom speaks at meetings.|Such chances come along very seldom.
column6: happening at long intervals – 隔很久才发生一次
column7: 难得：不容易遇到|不常：发生的次数少

column2: 借自拉丁语 sēlēctiō（挑出），源自 sēligere（挑选），由 sē-（分开）＋ legere（拣取）构成
column3: the act of choosing, or a group of chosen things
column5: Her selection surprised the committee.|The shop offers a wide selection.
column6: picking some out and setting them apart – 挑出一部分另放一边
column7: 选择：挑选这个行为|精选品：挑出来的那一批

column2: 古英语 self／seolf ← 原始日耳曼语 *selbaz ← 原始印欧语 *selbʰ-（自身的）
column3: a person as the subject of their own thoughts
column5: She wrote about her younger self.|He seems his old self again.
column6: the person considered as their own subject – 把人当作自身的那个主体
column7: 自我：作为思考主体的自身|本人：所说的就是那个人

column2: 由 self ＋ -ish 构成
column3: caring only about oneself and not others
column5: That was a selfish thing to do.|He is too selfish to share.
column6: turned only towards oneself – 只朝自身一面转的

column2: 古英语 sellan（交出、售出）← 原始西日耳曼语 *salljan ← 原始日耳曼语 *saljaną
column3: to give something in exchange for money
column5: They sell fresh bread every morning.|He sold the car last week.
column6: handing something over for money – 把东西交出去换钱
column7: 卖：把东西给出以换取钱|出售：正式对外发售

column2: 借自德语 Semester ← 新拉丁语 sēmestris（历时六个月），由 sex（六）＋ mēnsis（月）构成
column3: one of two divisions of an academic year
column5: The semester ends in early June.|She takes four courses this semester.
column6: a six-month stretch of study – 学业上以半年为一段的时段

column2: 借自德语 Seminar ← 拉丁语 sēminārium（苗圃），源自 sēmen（种子）
column3: a small class where a topic is discussed
column5: The seminar meets every Thursday afternoon.|She led a seminar on trade.
column6: a nursery bed where ideas are raised – 培育想法的苗床
column7: 研讨会：围绕专题讨论的聚会|专题课：小班研讨形式的课

column2: 中古英语 senat ← 古法语 senat ← 拉丁语 senātus（长老会议），源自 senex（年老）
column3: the upper house of a law-making body
column5: The senate voted late that night.|A senate committee reviewed the bill.
column6: a council of elders – 由年长者组成的议事会
column7: 参议院：两院制中的上院|元老院：古罗马的最高议事机构

column2: 借自拉丁语 senātor，源自 senex（年老），相当于 senate ＋ -or
column3: a member of a senate
column5: The senator spoke for twenty minutes.|Two senators opposed the change.
column6: one who sits in the council of elders – 在长老议事会中有席位的人

column2: 古英语 sendan ← 原始西日耳曼语 *sandijan ← 原始日耳曼语 *sandijaną
column3: to cause something to go to another place
column5: She sent the letter on Monday.|Please send someone to help us.
column6: causing something to travel away – 使某物离开此处前往别处
column7: 送出：使某物离开此处发往别处|寄：通过邮递发出

column2: 中古英语 senior ← 拉丁语 senior（较年长的），为 senex（年老）的比较级
column3: older or higher in rank, or a person of higher rank
column5: She is senior to me by two years.|Seniors met before the others arrived.
column6: standing higher by age or rank – 在年岁或职级上居上的
column7: 年长的：年纪或资历较大|上级：职级较高的人

column2: 古法语 sentement ← 拉丁语 sentimentum，源自 sentīre（感觉）
column3: a feeling or opinion about something
column5: The letter expressed real sentiment.|Public sentiment turned against the plan.
column6: what one feels rather than reasons out – 由感受而非推理得出的东西
column7: 情感：心里生出的感受|意见：由此形成的看法

column2: 借自拉丁语 September，源自 septem（七）——罗马旧历以三月为岁首，故为第七个月
column3: the ninth month of the year
column5: The term starts in early september.|September brought cooler evenings this year.
column6: once the seventh month of the year – 旧历里排第七的那个月

column2: 由 series ＋ -al 构成，仿拉丁语 seriālis；series ← 拉丁语 seriēs（接连）
column3: arranged in a sequence, or a story told in parts
column5: Each part carries a serial number.|The radio serial ran for years.
column6: coming one after another in line – 一个接一个排下来的
column7: 顺序的：按先后次序排列的|连载：分次刊出的作品

column2: 借自拉丁语 seriēs，源自 serere（接连、串起）
column3: a number of similar things coming one after another
column5: The museum owns a series of prints.|A series of delays followed.
column6: things strung together in a row – 串成一行的一批东西
column7: 系列：同类事物成组的一批|连续：一个接一个不间断

column2: 中古英语 seryows ← 古法语 serieux ← 中世纪拉丁语 sēriōsus，为拉丁语 sērius（郑重）的扩展形
column3: not joking, or giving cause for concern
column5: He gave me a serious look.|The injury proved more serious.
column6: weighty enough to demand attention – 重到必须当真对待
column7: 严肃的：认真不轻率|严重的：后果重大令人担心

column2: 由动词短语 set back 转成名词
column3: a problem that delays or reverses progress
column5: The storm was a serious setback.|They met one setback after another.
column6: being pushed back from where one had got – 从已到之处被推回去
column7: 挫折：使进展受阻的打击|倒退：进度退回到先前状态

column2: 由 set ＋ -ing 构成
column3: the place and conditions in which something happens
column5: The novel has a rural setting.|Adjust the setting before printing.
column6: the frame within which something is placed – 某事被安放进去的那个框架
column7: 环境：事情发生的场所与条件|背景：故事所设定的时地

column2: 古英语 setlan（安置、使坐定）与 sahtlian（调停）两支合流，前者出 setl（座）
column3: to come to rest, or to bring a matter to an end
column5: Dust settled on the empty shelves.|They settled the dispute quietly.
column6: coming to rest in a fixed place – 落定在一个不再动的位置
column7: 沉降：颗粒或物体落到底部|解决：把纠纷或问题了结
